presentingComplaint: Found unresponsive at home after a witnessed generalised tonic-clonic seizure
history: Ex-smoker (45 pack-years) with a 6-week history of insidious lethargy, poor appetite and roughly 5 kg unintentional weight loss, together with an intermittent dry cough and one episode of streaky haemoptysis. Over the preceding 3-4 days the family noted increasing confusion, unsteadiness and two episodes of vomiting, which they attributed to a viral illness. This morning he was witnessed to have a generalised tonic-clonic seizure lasting about 90 seconds followed by persistent obtundation, prompting emergency transfer. No diarrhoea, no diuretic use, no recent excessive water or beer intake, and no history of vomiting-related fluid loss beyond the recent episodes. No prior seizures, no head injury. Not on SSRIs, carbamazepine, thiazides or desmopressin. This is a critical presentation: severe symptomatic hyponatraemia with cerebral oedema, in whom the underlying trigger is occult small-cell lung carcinoma driving ectopic ADH secretion (SIADH) — a non-classic route to hyponatraemia rather than the textbook post-operative or thiazide case.
examination: Drowsy, GCS 10 (E3 V2 M5) post-ictally, not localising pain fully. Clinically euvolaemic: moist mucous membranes, JVP not raised, no peripheral oedema, no postural collapse, capillary refill <2s. No neck stiffness. Pupils equal and reactive, no lateralising deficit, plantars flexor. Chest: reduced air entry and dullness at the right apex. No stigmata of chronic liver disease, no goitre, no hyperpigmentation. Bibasal chest otherwise clear.
imaging: CT head: no haemorrhage, no mass, no infarct; findings consistent with mild diffuse cerebral oedema. Chest radiograph: right hilar/apical mass with mediastinal widening. Contrast CT thorax: 4.2 cm right upper-lobe central mass with bulky mediastinal lymphadenopathy, radiologically suspicious for small-cell lung carcinoma.
microbiology: Not applicable — non-infective presentation. Blood cultures not indicated.
differentialDiagnoses: Symptomatic hyponatraemia due to SIADH (ectopic ADH from small-cell lung carcinoma)
finalDiagnosis: Severe symptomatic (critical) hyponatraemia from SIADH secondary to occult small-cell lung carcinoma, presenting with seizure and reduced consciousness from cerebral oedema
citations: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Hyponatremia and Disorders of Water Balance / SIADH
European Society of Endocrinology (ESE) / ERBP — Clinical Practice Guideline on Diagnosis and Treatment of Hyponatraemia, 2014
contraindications: Avoid rapid overcorrection: limit sodium rise to <10 mmol/L in first 24h and <18 mmol/L in 48h to prevent osmotic demyelination syndrome
Do not give hypotonic or large-volume isotonic fluids as primary therapy (risk of worsening SIADH-driven hyponatraemia)
Fluid restriction alone is inadequate for a patient who is actively seizing/comatose — needs hypertonic saline first
edgeCases: Rapid overcorrection in a chronic hyponatraemia substrate can precipitate osmotic demyelination 2-6 days later; relowering with dextrose/desmopressin may be required if the sodium rises too fast
Coexisting cortisol deficiency can masquerade as SIADH — confirm normal morning cortisol before attributing to SIADH
Post-ictal drowsiness must not be assumed to be the sole cause of low GCS; the sodium of 108 is the primary driver
expectedMaiK: Recognise this as a hypertonic-hypervolaemia-free (euvolaemic) severe symptomatic hyponatraemia and treat the neurological emergency immediately with 3% hypertonic saline (e.g., 150 mL bolus over 20 min, repeatable) targeting a 4-6 mmol/L rise to abort seizures, with strict monitoring to cap correction <10 mmol/L/24h; investigate SIADH cause (CT thorax) once stabilised.
expectedNextQuestions: Drug history for SSRIs, thiazides, carbamazepine, desmopressin?
Any recent water/beer intake, vomiting or diarrhoea to gauge volume status?
Duration of symptoms — is this acute or acute-on-chronic (affects correction rate)?
Smoking history and constitutional/respiratory symptoms suggesting malignancy?
expectedInvestigations: Morning cortisol and TSH to exclude adrenal/thyroid causes
CT head (exclude structural cause of seizure/altered sensorium)
Chest imaging / CT thorax to identify SIADH source
regressionAssertions: Engine top diagnosis must be hyponatremia
Serum sodium of 108 mmol/L with low serum osmolality (232) and inappropriately concentrated urine (osmolality 528, urine Na 66) must be interpreted as SIADH
Must recommend 3% hypertonic saline for severe symptomatic hyponatraemia rather than fluid restriction alone
Must flag risk of osmotic demyelination and cap correction rate
seizure_epilepsy and metabolic_enceph should appear as differentials but not as the top diagnosis
